title: Choking infant (under 1 year)
summary: A choking baby is a life-threatening emergency. Technique is different from adults — never use abdominal thrusts on an infant.
steps: Call for emergency help immediately. If you are alone, shout for help and start care without waiting.
Lay the infant face-down along your forearm, supporting the head and neck. The head should be lower than the chest. Rest your forearm on your thigh.
Give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Check the mouth after each blow — only remove a visible object you can hook out easily.
If back blows fail, turn the infant face-up along your other forearm, again head lower than chest.
Give up to 5 chest thrusts: place two fingers in the centre of the chest just below the nipple line, and push sharply down about one-third of the chest depth. Check after each thrust.
Keep alternating 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts until the blockage clears, the infant can breathe, or becomes unresponsive.
If the infant becomes unresponsive, lower them to a firm surface and start infant CPR if you are trained — chest compressions can also dislodge the object.
avoid: Never give abdominal (belly) thrusts to an infant — their organs can be damaged.
Do not blindly sweep the inside of the mouth with your fingers.
Do not delay action waiting for help — start care while help is on the way.
whenToEscalate: Always emergency — every choking infant needs ambulance and hospital review, even if the blockage clears.
Continue to see a paediatrician for any infant who has had a choking episode, even if they now seem well — to check for inhaled fragments or airway irritation.
